% English cover letter (standard letter class, XeLaTeX): a job, fellowship or
% program application, or a manuscript-submission letter to a journal editor.
% Keep it to one page. State only real facts about yourself and your work.
\documentclass[11pt]{letter}

\usepackage[a4paper,margin=2.5cm]{geometry}
\usepackage[hidelinks]{hyperref}

% Sender block, printed at the top right.
\address{Your Name \\
  Street Address \\
  City, Postal Code, Country \\
  \href{mailto:your.name@example.org}{your.name@example.org}}
\signature{Your Name}
% Write the sending date; \today would print the date this version was first
% built (the build clock is pinned per snapshot for reproducibility).
\date{Month DD, YYYY}

\begin{document}

% Recipient block: name/role, organization, postal address.
\begin{letter}{Hiring Committee \\
  Department or Organization \\
  Street Address \\
  City, Postal Code, Country}

\opening{Dear Members of the Hiring Committee,}

% Paragraph 1: the position (or the manuscript title and target journal) and
% a one-sentence summary of why you are a strong fit.
I am writing to apply for the position of Position Title at Organization.

% Paragraph 2: two or three concrete, verifiable achievements that match the
% role's requirements (for a journal: the contribution and why it fits the
% journal's scope).
State the most relevant experience or contribution here.

% Paragraph 3: why this organization or journal specifically, and what you
% would bring to it.
Explain your motivation and fit here.

% Closing paragraph: availability, enclosed documents, thanks.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to hearing from you.

\closing{Sincerely,}

\encl{Curriculum vitae}

\end{letter}

\end{document}
